note: *** USER SYMPTOM (2026-10-15, device in hand): no display; volume keys and audio NORMAL; but the POWER KEY CANNOT CONTROL BACKLIGHT (contrast s3/armA where the power key DID control it, 160->511). *** Sample 4 = CONTROL ARM (baseline m1-baseline-f3 = boot_b), true physical POR, normal disk boot. CLASSIC Q28 BAD BOOT: l1=5 (command DMA timeout status=0x2200200 + peer timeout + 'bonded command DMA failed master=-110 peer=-110' + 'Failed to initialize panel -110' at 12.23s), l2=389, 'ctl reset failure'=172, dsi_isr=0. FALSE-GOOD TRAP REPEATED: card0-DSI-1=connected, phoc/phosh/wayland all up, backlight=511, DPMS On - all normal while panel is dark. CRITICAL: this gives the CONTROL arm a bad sample in the SAME session, which is exactly what makes the arm A comparison meaningful. dsi_isr remains consistent as auxiliary discriminator: 41 when user-confirmed lit (s2), 0 when bad (s4 here, s1, s3). RUNNING TALLY: armA 0 GOOD/2 BAD ; baseline 1 GOOD/1 BAD => SAME RATE (~50%), consistent with the standing '~50% clustered, image-independent' understanding. This MATERIALLY WEAKENS the earlier directional reading that 'arm A is worse' and, more importantly, means arm A's failures are NOT distinguishable from baseline's failures.
